# Results — Study 791 (Advertising-Brand-Capital)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The **brand-capital premium**
(Belo-Lin-Vitorino 2014; Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis 2001): rank a consumer basket each month
by **advertising intensity** (AdvertisingExpense / Sales), go **long the heavy advertisers /
short the light**, rebalance monthly with a one-year reporting lag and one execution lag, and
race the spread against SPY and a label-shuffle placebo. `REAL` needs a **positive** HAC
`t >= 2` **and** placebo survival. Offline & deterministic from the cache; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (last complete
month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `979148cad57d` (advertising +
revenue + returns panels).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Fundamentals tape | **SEC EDGAR** companyconcept — annual `AdvertisingExpense` (9 of 46 names file the broader `MarketingAndAdvertisingExpense` tag instead) + revenue; 10-K full-year facts, consolidated total per fiscal year |
| Price / return tape | yfinance monthly **total return** (auto-adjusted close); public, no key |
| Window | **2010-02 → 2026-06** (197 signal months; **196** holding months after the execution lag; 16.4 years) |
| Field | **46** consumer large-caps that file the advertising line; advertising coverage **≈ 88%** of name-years (767/874), FY 2008-2026 |
| Signal | **advertising / sales**, formed monthly: AdvertisingExpense(FY Y-1) ÷ Revenue(FY Y-1) |
| Formation / costs | **monthly** rebalance, top/bottom **tertile**, **1-yr reporting lag** + **1-month execution lag** (signal at month *t* selects the book entered next month); 10 bps one-way turnover + **100 bps/yr borrow** on the short leg |

> **Scope caveats (named on the Signal axis).** *Coverage* — the advertising line is **not**
> a required disclosure post-ASU-2014, so the vast majority of US firms omit it; even inside
> this consumer basket some large advertisers (McDonald's, Costco, Estée Lauder, Booking,
> Hilton) never file it and are excluded. The tested universe is *the set of firms that
> disclose advertising*, a selected slice, not the market. *Concept heterogeneity* — 9 names
> file `MarketingAndAdvertisingExpense` (marketing + advertising bundled), which mildly
> over-states pure advertising for them. *Survivorship* — current-membership consumer basket
> projected back to 2010; both legs (heavy-advertising staples, light-advertising retail) are
> survivors, so the tilt is largely common to both legs of the long/short.

The long (heavy advertisers) and short (light advertisers) tertiles as of the final-month signal:

- **Long (heavy advertisers):** CHD, CL, CLX, CMCSA, DECK, DIS, DPZ, EBAY, ETSY, EXPE, KO, NKE, PG, STZ, TAP
- **Short (light advertisers):** BBY, CAG, CMG, F, HD, LOW, ROST, SBUX, SJM, T, TGT, TJX, VZ, WMT, YUM

Advertising intensity spans two orders of magnitude — digital marketplaces (ETSY 27.4%,
EXPE 26.5%) and classic brand builders (CL 13.3%, CHD/DPZ/KO ~11%) at the top; big-box and
off-price retail (ROST 0.33%, WMT/HD 0.75%, TJX 1.1%) at the bottom.

## The race — heavy-advertiser long, light-advertiser short, vs the market

Equal-weight, monthly rebalanced; CAGR / annualised Sharpe / max drawdown over the 196 holding months.

| book | CAGR | Sharpe | max drawdown | mean (ann) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Long — heavy advertisers (top tertile) | 12.81% | 0.92 | −28.2% | +13.12% |
| **Short — light advertisers (bottom tertile)** | **16.17%** | **1.11** | −22.3% | **+16.13%** |
| **Long − short (the advertising spread)** | **−3.32%** | **−0.35** | −45.9% | **−3.00%** |
| S&P 500 (SPY) | 14.56% | 1.02 | −23.9% | +14.71% |

The **light** advertisers out-earn the heavy advertisers *and* the market — the exact opposite
of the brand-capital claim. The long-short (heavy minus light) is **negative**.

## The Signal-axis test — HAC t-stats

Newey-West HAC t of the monthly spread (the desk's `REAL` needs a **positive** `t >= 2` **and**
placebo survival):

| spread | mean | HAC t | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Long − short (advertising spread)** | **−3.00%/yr** | **−1.46** | 196 |
| Long (heavy) − SPY | −1.47%/yr | −0.62 | 196 |
| Short (light) − SPY | +1.54%/yr | +0.65 | 196 |

The advertising long-short is **−3.00%/yr at t = −1.46** — the wrong sign for the claim and
inside the noise. Decomposed, **neither leg** does anything distinguishable from the market:
the heavy leg is −1.47%/yr vs SPY (t = −0.62), the light leg +1.54%/yr vs SPY (t = +0.65).
There is no brand premium — in either direction — on this tape.

## Placebo — does the *signal* carry any return axis? (it does not)

Permute the advertising-intensity labels across names (same values, wrong names) and rebuild
the long-short, 300 draws:

| | annualised long-short spread |
|---|--:|
| Advertising long-short (this study) | −3.00%/yr |
| Shuffled-label null — mean | −0.18%/yr |
| Shuffled-label null — std dev | 2.34%/yr |
| Advertising spread percentile in the null | 13.3 |
| **Placebo two-sided p** | **0.20** |

The observed spread sits at the **13th percentile** of the shuffled null (two-sided **p =
0.20**) — *not* in the tail. Unlike study 525's R&D/ME (which at least survived its placebo as
a real value axis), advertising intensity here loads on **no** reliable cross-sectional return
axis: a random relabelling pays about the same. The negative sign is style noise (defensive
staples lagged retail over 2010-2026), not a signal.

## Robustness — long/short fraction

| split | long-short | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| top/bottom **half** | −0.68%/yr | −0.41 |
| top/bottom **tertile** (headline) | −3.00%/yr | −1.46 |
| top/bottom **quartile** | −3.47%/yr | −1.33 |
| top/bottom **quintile** | −2.24%/yr | −0.81 |

No sort width rescues it — the spread is negative and sub-2 (in absolute value) everywhere,
with no concentrated tail where a hidden premium lives.

## Costs + short-borrow — a moot check

Advertising intensity is a slow annual characteristic, so turnover is tiny (~1.0% one-way per
month); the only material friction is short-borrow.

| | gross | net (10 bps turnover + 100 bps/yr borrow on the short) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Long-short spread** | **−3.00%/yr (t = −1.46)** | **−4.00%/yr (t = −1.94)** |

Borrow makes a negative spread more negative. The point is academic: there is no positive edge
to erode, and one does not allocate to a wrong-signed, insignificant book.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, the tape is just null

A deterministic monthly panel (fixed seed, 15 years × 40 names) where the first half are
persistently heavy advertisers, market beta is common to both legs, and a knob `edge` plants
the *true* annual heavy-minus-light premium:

| planted edge | recovered long-short spread | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| `edge = 0.00` (no true premium) | +0.47%/yr | **+0.18** |
| `edge = 0.06` (large +6%/yr premium) | +6.47%/yr | **+2.47** |
| `edge = 0.08` (+8%/yr premium) | +8.47%/yr | **+3.23** |
| null across **20 seeds** (edge = 0) | mean t **−0.22** (sd 0.43), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20** |  |

With no planted premium the long-short is flat and insignificant (the harness never
manufactures a false positive across 20 seeds); a planted +6%/yr premium is cleanly recovered
at `t ≈ 2.5`. The engine finds a premium **only** where one is planted — so the real-tape
`t = −1.46` is a **true null**, not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed brand premium is a *positive* one; the advertising long-short
  is **−3.00%/yr at HAC t = −1.46** (wrong sign, and inside the noise), fails the placebo
  (13th percentile, p = 0.20), is negative and sub-2 at every sort width, and **neither leg
  beats SPY**. The literature (Belo-Lin-Vitorino; Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) reports a brand/
  intangible premium; this clean, point-in-time, disclosure-limited tape cannot certify it. A
  positive-t literature result plus a negative-and-insignificant tape ⇒ **NONE**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A wrong-signed, insignificant spread is nothing to allocate to;
  net of 10 bps turnover + 100 bps/yr short-borrow it is −4.00%/yr (t = −1.94), and the
  turnover is trivial (~1.0%/month) precisely because the signal barely moves.

> **One-line.** Sort a basket of ad-disclosing consumer names by advertising/sales and the
> heavy advertisers *lag* the light ones by −3.00%/yr (HAC t = −1.46) — the wrong sign for the
> brand-capital premium, failing the placebo (p = 0.20) and every sort width, with neither leg
> beating the market: no brand premium on this tape, just the decade's staples-vs-retail style
> weather blowing through a signal that carries no information of its own.
